answer:
Password cracking primarily involves an adversary attempting to guess a password by trying every possible combination until successful. This method is known as a brute force attack. It is feasible computationally and guarantees success as it systematically goes through all potential passwords based on the defined alphabet (including lower case letters, upper case letters, numbers, and symbols) and the maximum password length [Source 1].

Adversaries may employ brute force techniques when they do not know the password or when they have obtained password hashes. They can systematically guess the password using a repetitive or iterative mechanism, often interacting with a service that checks the validity of the credentials [Source 2].

## Attack description

An adversary tries every possible value for a password until they succeed. A brute force attack, if feasible computationally, will always be successful because it will essentially go through all possible passwords given the alphabet used (lower case letters, upper case letters, numbers, symbols, etc.) and the maximum length of the password.

## Execution flow
